diagnoses.label: Incomplete equal-contribution footnote pattern coverage
diagnoses.general_pattern: Skill lists 'Equal contribution' as a pattern to redact but only shows two exact-string examples ('Equal contribution', '* Equal contribution'). It does not enumerate common typographic variants (e.g., asterisk without space, dagger/double-dagger markers, superscript symbols, 'These authors contributed equally', 'Co-first authors') nor instruct agents to search for the phrase 'equal contribution' case-insensitively / as a substring. Agents following the literal example may build a redaction list that misses variants actually present in papers.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: Verifier failed test_identifiers_redacted with 'paper3.pdf: identifiers not redacted: ["Equal contribution"]'. Trajectory shows the extracted text contains '*Equal contribution' (asterisk directly adjacent, no space) on page 0 of paper3, and the agent's leak-check regex list did not include any 'equal contribution' pattern, so it was never added to the redaction list.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: A required step to (a) always search for the case-insensitive substring 'equal contribution' (and common marker variants like *, †, ‡, superscripts) rather than a single exact string, and (b) verify post-redaction that no form of 'equal contribution' text remains before declaring success.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Expand the 'Equal contribution footnotes' guidance to require substring / case-insensitive detection of the phrase plus enumeration of typical marker prefixes, and add a verification check that scans redacted output for any remaining 'equal contribution' occurrence, treating any hit as a failure to fix.
diagnoses.target_section: Patterns to Redact (Before References Only) — item 8 'Equal contribution footnotes'

diagnoses.label: Verification step lacks identifier-leak scan
diagnoses.general_pattern: The REQUIRED verification function only checks structural integrity (page count, character retention). It does not verify that the categories of identifying information the skill itself enumerates (author names, affiliations, emails, arXiv IDs, DOIs, venues, equal-contribution notes) are actually absent from the redacted pre-references text. Agents therefore can pass 'verification' while leakage persists.
diagnoses.observable_evidence: The agent's own custom leak-scan (built ad hoc) did not include an 'equal contribution' pattern, and the skill-provided verify_redaction() would not have caught it either — it prints '✓ Verification passed' based only on length ratios. The run ended with the agent declaring success while an identifier still leaked, causing test_identifiers_redacted to fail.
diagnoses.missing_reasoning_step: A leak-audit step in verification that, for each pattern category listed in 'Patterns to Redact', re-scans the redacted document's pre-references pages and raises on any remaining match.
diagnoses.correct_general_approach: Extend the verification contract to include a per-category residual-leak check driven by the same pattern taxonomy the skill defines, so structural checks and content-leak checks are both mandatory before considering redaction complete.

package_assessment.rationale: The failure is a single leaked identifier ('Equal contribution' on paper3) that maps directly to two gaps in the academic-pdf-redaction skill: (1) the equal-contribution pattern guidance is under-specified and example-driven rather than substring/variant-driven, and (2) the mandated verification routine only checks length/structure and does not audit for residual identifier categories the skill itself enumerates. Both gaps are reusable, skill-controllable, and jointly explain why the agent believed the task was complete.
